purpose: Bind a bounded capability mid-training comparison that measures data value and downstream optimization efficiency from a useful parent checkpoint.
research_basis: The MidTool review in docs/research.md motivates separating raw source, grounded augmentation and executable trajectory supervision while holding downstream post-training fixed.

common_contract.parent: One useful 4K production checkpoint, with model tensors and optimizer state hash-bound before branching. No arm may start without a qualified parent.
common_contract.continuation: A changed-data continuation contract must be implemented and qualified before launch. Do not relabel a data intervention as context extension.
common_contract.objective: Next-token prediction with identical serialization, masking and optimizer policy across arms.
common_contract.exposure: Matched complete-update tokens and schedule across arms; report source exposure and replay separately. Mid-training exposure remains part of the 100B working horizon, not an additional allowance.
common_contract.initialization: Arms branch from the same useful parent and preserve the declared optimizer policy. Any cursor reset or optimizer-state change is predeclared and measured.
common_contract.downstream: Use one fixed SFT recipe and one fixed RL feasibility recipe for linked efficiency evaluation. Downstream runs are charged to the 150-hour post-training research reservation, not hidden in this packet.
common_contract.evaluation: Hold out source families and final tests. Report source/domain loss, capability, retention, SFT convergence and early RL adaptation separately.
common_contract.accounting: Count source preparation, teacher/generation, validation, retries, discarded trajectories, training, evaluation and allocated idle time once and by stage.

arms.role: Preceding-stage data and broad replay control
arms.contract: Use the preceding-stage mixture under the same 4K next-token objective and matched exposure. This controls for continuation compute and parent age.
Add qualified code, math, repair and tool-facing documentation with no synthesized QA or trajectories. Keep broad replay and total exposure fixed against the control.
Add validated source-grounded QA or workflow supervision to the raw targeted route. Preserve the originating context, teacher identity, generation settings and rejection reasons.
required_evidence: held-out family separation for source and derived records

conditional_branch.replacement_scope: May replace grounded_targeted only after tool environments, schemas, turn order, required arguments, responses, recovery cases and verifier reliability are qualified.
conditional_branch.reason: The 150-hour mid-training reservation cannot support an undeclared fourth arm. Preserve the branch as a recorded revision or later post-training study if environment cost is not affordable.

screening.order: Run the replay control and only candidates whose source, derivation and validation gates pass. Protect confirmation and linked downstream evaluation reservations.
screening.primary_evidence: Capability and source/domain loss at matched mid-training exposure, with retention and preparation cost.
screening.efficiency_evidence: Compare capability per mid-training token and GPU-hour, plus the downstream SFT convergence curve under the fixed recipe.
screening.failure_rule: If targeted data does not improve the predeclared endpoint or worsens retention/cost, retain the eligible replay control or record an explicit redesign.

confirmation.selected_candidate: One screening candidate, or a documented control-only/inconclusive outcome.
confirmation.controls: Same useful parent identity, declared optimizer policy, exposure, validation, downstream SFT recipe and final-test boundary.
confirmation.claim_boundary: One paired confirmation seed supports a bounded data/optimization result, not a global mixture optimum or guaranteed scaling law.

includes: retries, recovery and allocated idle time

linked_downstream_evaluation.fixed_sft: Same SFT data, masks, supervised-token exposure, optimizer, schedule and evaluation identities for every retained mid-training arm.
linked_downstream_evaluation.rl_feasibility: Same prompts, environment, verifier, rollout budget and recovery policy; report early adaptation and held-out transfer rather than in-environment reward alone.
efficiency_outputs: SFT loss area and steps to a fixed development target
Capability at matched SFT tokens and allocated GPU-hours
Early RL reward adaptation, final held-out transfer and rollout cost
Teacher, verifier, environment and discarded-output accounting
linked_downstream_evaluation.boundary: Linked downstream evaluation is required to make an optimization-efficiency claim, but it is not additional mid-training exposure and cannot be silently charged to the 150-hour mid-training reservation.

required_gates_before_first_arm: Useful parent checkpoint, model/optimizer identities and changed-data continuation contract are hash-bound.
Selected source families pass source-use, exact/near-duplicate, benchmark and held-out partition gates.
Accepted unique tokens, replay exposure, derivation lineage and preparation cost are finite and recorded.
Grounded or executable supervision has independent correctness, schema, response and failure checks.
SFT/RL downstream data, environments, verifiers and evaluation identities are fixed before mid-training results are selected.
GH200 cost and recovery behavior support the matched horizon within the declared reservation.
required_outputs_for_report: Per-arm source, derived-example and replay accounting.
Capability and retention versus mid-training tokens and GPU-hours.
SFT convergence, early RL adaptation and held-out transfer under fixed downstream recipes.
Teacher, environment, validation, retry, idle and discarded-data costs.
Negative, inconclusive and conditional-branch outcomes with the same detail as selected results.
boundary: No arm is launch-ready from this packet. It defines a data and optimization study only; a future launch must bind the useful parent, changed-data implementation, admitted manifests, downstream packet, runtime measurements and an explicit launch receipt.
